tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

tools.description:

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). content.text:
I pulled the main checkout of JusPrin. It was already up to date with `jusprin-dev` (latest commit `e8aee03faf`), and nothing has changed since the handoff was written. I read the note, and I think I understand the work. Here it is in my own words so you can correct me.

**The issue.** The rule is that each failure goes to whoever can do something about it:
- **The person's failure** (their key, their folder, their account) is shown in words they can act on. If the other side already wrote such words, we show them as "X says: …".
- **Our failure** stops the work, travels up unchanged, and is reported by the one handler at the entry point.
- **A failure at a service the person chose** that is down is told truthfully and not reported.

Three code readers found 50 places where a failure goes to the wrong one.

**What happened.** The first attempt changed about 120 files at once and broke worse things than it fixed:
- edits were lost while the header said "Saved";
- a File menu click could end the app;
- a reply could be had without paying.

All of it was reversed. Three mistakes led there:
- deciding by error number instead of by cause;
- calling ordinary user mistakes "ours";
- throwing where nothing above reports it.

The second pass approved 17 simple places. Six were changed, two of them only in part, and pushed. The other eleven were left, mostly because their failure couldn't be made to happen.

**How to continue.** For each place, one at a time:
1. Decide whose failure it is from what the other side actually says.
2. Make the failure happen in the real app or on the real local server.
3. Make the change only if it's an added or removed try/catch or if/else, or deleted handling.
4. If it needs anything more (a new sentence, a new field, a change in OrcaSlicer's own code, a memory of what was already reported), don't build it. Bring it to you.

Before making a failure "ours", I'd also check that a person can't reach it by doing something ordinary, and name the handler above the throw that reports it.

**Checks against the code:**
- The password sign-in branch is still at `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:311-312`: any 400 on login becomes "That password is wrong."
- The repeat check in `report_unexpected` (`Support/ErrorReport.cpp`) really does run only on the dialog path. With automatic reports on, the report is sent before the check, so every repeat goes out. That supports the note's unapproved idea of applying that one check to both paths.
- The notes folder has every file the handoff names.

**Where I'd start.** The best next place is "shipped profiles fail during an import from OrcaSlicer" (`Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:229-231` and `:341-345`). The same failure was already made to happen for the printer setup form, so it should be easy to make happen here too. The change would be the same simple rethrow.

Should I start with the OrcaSlicer import's shipped-profiles failure, or pick another place?

Kenneth Jiang Wed Nov 25 10:51:21 2026 -0800

A refusal from a person's own AI service is shown in the service's words; outages, an offline sign-out and unreadable shipped profiles go to whoever can act on them

These places sent a failure to the wrong one, by the Error handling rules in
AGENTS.md. Each was made to happen in the built app before it was changed, and
again after.

A person's own AI service refuses and says why. JusPrin 2.0.1 answered
"Something went wrong on our side" and sent us a report nobody here could act
on. The report that started this work came from the key check: a person's
OpenRouter workspace took only their own provider keys, and OpenRouter
answered 404 with words that said what to do and gave the address. The app
now shows the other side's own words after its name, in one line of text:

    OpenRouter says: “No endpoints found that can be served by your own
    provider keys. … Add provider keys at https://openrouter.ai/…”

Kenneth approved the form on 2026-11-24: "Name, then its words". The words
stay in the language they came in, and only the message text is shown. The
line is one translatable string, translated in the 22 catalogs.

It is shown in three places, and none of them is reported:
- The key check in Preferences and in first-run setup, for any refusal that
  carries words. The key check sends the same request for every person; only
  the key and its account differ.
- A chat on a person's own key, for a 403 that carries words (a country the
  service does not serve, a spending limit, input its moderation flagged) and
  for a 429 that carries words, which can name a daily cap. A 429 with no
  words keeps "The <service> service is rate limited. Try again shortly."
  A 400, 404 or 422 on a chat stays ours: we build that request, and a
  malformed one cannot be told from a refusal.
- Exporting kept G-code from Print history into a folder the system refuses,
  such as a locked or full card. The app used to report it as ours and show
  nothing. It now shows "macOS says: “/Volumes/CARD: Read-only file system”"
  under "Couldn't export G-code". A failure about any other path is still

commit 29445fd705b04b8374d0f016b431de811b92b2e7
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 25 10:53:03 2026 -0800

    JusPrin 2: refused app requests and a failed card lookup come to us; a signed-out browser at checkout is told what to do
    
    Three places sent a failure to the wrong one, by the Error handling rules in
    CLAUDE.md. Each was made to happen on the local server before it was changed.
    
    A request the app sends that the server refuses. The AI gateway answered 400
    "The request is not valid." or "This model is not available." and logged one
    info line; a print report with no G-code hash, an unknown outcome or facts
    that are not JSON answered 400 the same way. The app writes every one of
    these requests after signing in, so a refusal is a mistake of ours on one end
    or the other, and we never heard of it. They now raise, so the answer is 500
    "Something went wrong on our side" and the error is reported. The app already
    showed that sentence for these answers, so a person sees no change. The web
    link address is left as it was: it also answers a signed-out app, with no
    token, so the sender is not known to be the app.
    
    The card line on Billing and usage. Any failure from Chargebee was read as
    "no card on file". A customer Chargebee does not have still means no card,
    which is normal for an account with no customer on JusPrin 2's site. Any other
    answer, such as a refused key, now raises. On a server with no key for that
    site, which includes local development, Billing and usage for a paid account
    now answers 500 where it used to show no card.
    
    A browser no longer signed in at checkout. Pressing a buy button in a tab left
    open past its sign-in, or coming back from paying in one, went to Credits and
    plans with nothing said. Both now show the existing page "This link has
    expired. Go back to JusPrin and open the page again." with status 410 and a
    log line. It is the person's, so it is not reported. What they paid for is
    added by Chargebee's webhook, as before.

     """"Visa ending 4242", or None when Chargebee has no card for the account."""
     try:
         card = chargebee.Customer.retrieve(customer_id(user), env=_site()).card
-    except chargebee.APIError:
+    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
+        # An account that paid without a customer on this site, such as a
+        # plan bought before it had its own, has no card here. Anything else
+        # Chargebee answers is ours.
+        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
+            raise
         return None
     if card is None:
         return None

     if len(text) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MIN_TEXT:

     photos = request.FILES.getlist('photos')

+    if user is None:
+        # Back from paying in a browser no longer signed in: the person's. The
+        # webhook adds what they bought, which they see in JusPrin.
+        LOGGER.info('JusPrin 2 checkout came back to a browser no longer signed in')
+        return render(request, 'jusprin/v2/sign_in_result.html', {
+            'heading': _('This link has expired'),
+            'line': _('Go back to JusPrin and open the page again.'),
+        }, status=410)
+    bought = billing.finish_checkout(user, request.GET['id']) if request.GET.get('id') else None
     if bought is None:

7-## Opening pull requests
8-
9:The `obico-server` submodule is the public, open-source repo. When you open a pull request against it, **target the `master` branch, not `release`.** The `release` branch is for end users and release builds; don't open contributor PRs against it unless a maintainer explicitly asks. See obico-server's [CONTRIBUTING.md](./obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full PR process.
10-
11:## Releases
12-
13:This repo's `release` branch is generated from `master`. Never commit to it directly: the next release wipes that commit.
14-
15:`./release.sh` makes a release:
16-
17-1. Pushes `master` of both `obico-server` and this repo. Every local commit on either `master` goes to GitHub.
18-2. Builds the frontend bundles.
19:3. Recreates `release` from `master` (`git checkout -B release master`), commits the bundles as "Check in built bundles", and force-pushes `release`.
20-
21:Every image is built from `release`:
22-
23:- **tsd and Elegoo (GKE).** CircleCI builds `web_ent` and `ml_api_ent` only for `release`. The images are tagged `obi.<CircleCI pipeline number>`, the number the ops manifests name.
24:- **Elegoo China.** ops `elegoo-cn/build-docker-img.sh <number>` runs `./aliyun.sh build <number> --push` on Aliyun's Shenzhen build machine. That script resets its copy of this repo to `origin/release`, so run `release.sh` first.
25-
26-Both builds run `git submodule update --remote`. The `obico-server` code in an image is therefore the head of obico-server's `master` when the build ran, not the commit this repo records for the submodule.
27-
28:To get a fix into an image, commit it on `master` and run `release.sh`.
29-
30-## Developing the frontend + backend locally
31-
32-The public repo is oriented around easy self-host running (it's primary purpose) but it's not currently setup to make it easy to develop.
33-This repo has config changes to make it possible to run the frontend and backend indipendantly to enable quick, iterative development.
34-
35-### Initial setup (one time only)
36-
----
#!/bin/bash -e

RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Trap to catch errors and display in red
trap 'exit_code=$?; trap - ERR; echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Command failed with exit code $exit_code${NC}" >&2; exit $exit_code' ERR

. $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh

# ── Preflight checks ──

echo "Running preflight checks..."

# Ensure obico-server is on master and push
cd obico-server
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! obico-server is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing obico-server..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push obico-server. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
cd ..

# Ensure tsd-enterprise is on master and push
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! tsd-enterprise is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing tsd-enterprise..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push tsd-enterprise. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

content.text:
The app commit and the server commits do what the handoff note says, place by place. One claim is out of date: the note says nothing on the server is deployed, but the server changes went out in a server release at 12:10 today. The note was last saved at 12:37, after that.

**App commit `e8aee03faf` (on `origin/jusprin-dev`).** Every item listed as done is in the diff:
- **The "X says" line.** `said_by` is in the new `Support/SaidBy.hpp`, and the string `%1% says: “%2%”` is translated in all 22 catalogs. The function only formats the line.
- **The key check.** A refusal under 500 that carries words is shown as the service's words and not reported. This applies only to the key-check request on a person's own key. There is a test that uses the real OpenRouter 404 text.
- **A chat on the person's own key.** A 403 with words and a 429 with words are shown in the service's words. A 429 with no words keeps the old rate-limit sentence. This path runs only for a person's own key, never for a JusPrin account. A 400, 404 or 408 still counts as ours, and the tests check that.
- **Exporting kept G-code.** Only a filesystem error that names the folder the person chose is shown, as "macOS says: <folder>: <reason>". Anything else is rethrown. The copy step names both the kept copy and the target, so the note's caveat holds: an unreadable kept copy would also be shown as the system's words. There is no unit test, as the note says.
- **An outage at the person's own AI service.** An answer of 500 or more, or an overload named inside a reply, now shows "The AI request could not reach the … service." and is not reported. This doesn't apply to a JusPrin account or a model on this computer. The models list does the same.
- **Signing out with no network.** It is only logged now. An error answer from our server is still reported.
- **Shipped printer profiles that can't be read.** The loader now throws, and the old sentence is gone from the source and the catalogs. The loader's only caller reads the profiles on a worker thread. The error comes back on two timers, the printer chat's and Home's, and both go through the reporting wrapper. So the throw is reported and can't end the app. `SetupOptions::error` is still sent to the form at `PrinterConversation.cpp:1547`, as the note says.

**Server commits.** The three commits the note names (`d9c224e114`, `29445fd705`, `f729e8524f`) are on `origin/master`. The code does what the note says:
- the gateway and print reports now raise on a request the app sent that the server refuses;
- the card lookup treats only Chargebee's `resource_not_found` as "no card";
- a signed-out browser at checkout, or coming back from paying, gets the "This link has expired" page with status 410.

**The deployment claim.** All three commits are also on `origin/release`, under a "Check in built bundles" commit from 12:10 today. That is what `release.sh` produces. The server README says CircleCI builds the production images only from `release`. So a production image with these changes was probably built. I haven't checked whether it is running in production. If it is, the note's warnings now apply to production, not just the local server:
- a paid account's Billing and usage page answers 500 when Chargebee refuses the key;
- refused app requests now raise and are reported.

Should I check whether the new server build is running in production — yes, or not now?

name: gateway-incident-lookup
description: "Where to look when JusPrin Cloud AI requests fail in production: log filter, Langfuse per-request records, where Sentry runs; what the gateway does not report"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: abfcedd2-d13e-4e49-b0b8-b888e8134103
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:04:48.653Z
---

How to investigate failed AI requests on the JusPrin Cloud gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), worked out 2026-11-14.

- **Log lines:** `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="tsd" AND textPayload:"JusPrin v2 upstream failure"' --project tsdtechnology`. Each line has the status, the upstream request id, the format and the alias. No user, no reason.
- **Per-request records:** Langfuse (us.cloud.langfuse.com; keys are in the `tsdws-prod` deployment's env). `GET /api/public/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION` (deprecated, v2 replaces it). `metadata` has `outcome`, `request_bytes`, `turn_id` (`p-<project>-c-<n>-m-<n>-attempt-<n>`), `request_kind`, `effort`, `alias`. This is what tells two people apart and shows Retry presses. `note` = a turn the app started itself.
- **Sentry server:** VM `sentry` in project `elegoo-backend` (us-central1-c), self-hosted docker behind Apache; the gateway reports to project 2. Serial console output (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`) shows container stops and starts. Apache answers 503 when the containers are down.
- **State on 2026-11-14 (check before relying on it):** the gateway sent to Sentry only upstream 401/403/404 and a failed chat save; the server's `LoggingIntegration` had `event_level=None`, so no log line became a Sentry event; the upstream error body was discarded; the desktop app had no remote error reporter at all, and showed an upstream 400 as "could not reach the service" with a Retry button.

Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]], [[jusprin-chat-capture-design]].

**Changed 2026-11-15 (tsd-enterprise 057ea6d412 on master; live only once deployed):** the gateway reports every unexpected upstream failure to Sentry with the provider's status, request id and error text, and the "JusPrin v2 upstream failure" log line is gone. Langfuse `outcome` then reads `failed <ExceptionType>` for reported failures, `upstream status N` only for 429/413/5xx, and metadata gains `upstream_request_id`. Check `git log` in tsd-enterprise before relying on either recipe.

**Changed 2026-11-18:** Langfuse's v1 `/api/public/observations` now answers 410 Gone. Use `GET /api/public/v2/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION&limit=1000&fields=core,basic,usage,metadata,model` and follow `meta.cursor`. Each record has `userId`, `usageDetails` (input, cache read, cache write by TTL, output) and `metadata`. The same Langfuse project also holds ~1,100 unrelated `OpenAI-generation` records (model gpt-6-luna, other users); keep only names starting `jusprin-v2-`. Working scripts: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cloud-usage/` (fetch2.py, analyze.py). See [[jusprin2-cloud-usage-per-user]].

But little JusPrin 2 traffic came in during that time, and the billing page and checkout weren't used at all, so most of the changed code hasn't been exercised by real users yet.

**Where I looked.** The production web, websocket and task servers all report to the `obico-server` project on sentry.obico.io. Four issues in that project were seen since the switch:
- **Ended-print and duplicate G-code file errors.** These are old Obico issues that keep recurring, and they have nothing to do with JusPrin.
- **`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'web_ent'` in `manage.py shell`.** This is new, seen once in a production pod. Someone opened a Django shell the wrong way. It isn't a request failure.
- **`'bool' object has no attribute 'lower'` at `/api/v1/octo/printer_events/`.** This is new, seen once, on the new build. A client sent `notify` as a JSON true where the code expects text, in a test message titled "System Health - JSON Push Test". The line that fails (`backend/api/octoprint_views.py:413` in obico-server) dates from 2023, so the new build didn't cause it.

No unresolved JusPrin issue was seen since the switch. The latest one is from 2026-11-24.

**JusPrin 2 traffic since the switch**, from the load balancer logs:
- 11 chat messages, all answered 200. So no request was refused, and the new rule that a refused request raises and is reported never had a chance to run.
- 25 account reads and 2 model-list reads, all 200, plus one 401 on each. A 401 is an ordinary signed-out client.
- One return from checkout (`web/done`, 200).
- No visits to Billing and usage, no checkout presses, and no real print reports. A few GET requests to POST-only addresses got 405s. They look like someone probing the addresses.
- No 500 anywhere on JusPrin 2.

**What's still unknown.** I can't tell whether production's Chargebee key for the JusPrin 2 site works. That decides whether Billing and usage shows the card or now answers 500, and the page hasn't been opened since the switch. It will show up in Sentry the first time a paid account opens it.

1	# Each misrouted failure: a simple change, or more (2026-11-25)
2	
3	Read only, on the app at `jusprin-dev` `9f485c3604` and the server at `master` `d9c224e114`. Nothing
4	was changed, built or run for this file. Each place in `error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` has one
5	entry, except the two Kenneth marked "Not to be fixed": the 120-second limit on a reply, and a
6	checkout that returns "succeeded" with the invoice unpaid. The list's place 21 holds seven separate
7	spots, and its places 26 and 27 hold two and four. Each of those spots has its own entry, so there are
8	50 entries in all. App paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, server paths under `web_ent/jusprin/`.
9	
10	"Simple" here is the reading in the brief, not Kenneth's wording. The change is made at the place
11	itself by adding or removing a try/catch or an if/else, or by deleting handling. It uses only what the
12	code has today.
13	
14	## Counts
15	
16	- **Simple: 17.**
17	- **Needs more: 30.**
18	- **Nothing to change: 3.**
19	- **Never made to happen: 34.** This counts across the three groups above. It means the failure
20	  itself was never produced against the real thing, by me or in the evidence I have. A test with a
21	  fake counts as never made to happen.
22	
23	The most common reasons a place needs more:
24	- the person's failure can only be told to them with words we do not have: a new sentence, or the
25	  "the system says" frame that went with the reversal;
26	- the failure repeats, every few seconds or on every press, so reporting it once needs a record of
27	  what was already reported;
28	- the page or callback gets only "worked or not", so telling "ours" apart from "no network" needs a
29	  new field.
30	
31	## The app
32	
33	**Credits and plans, Billing and usage, will not open.**
34	- Where: `Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:86-96`, the answer to the link request. Any answer other than 200 with a
35	  link, or no answer, shows "Couldn't load Credits and plans" (`:375`) with "Check your internet
36	  connection, then try again."
37	- Whose: an error answer from our server is ours, and no answer is the person's network. An ended
38	  sign-in (401) is the person's. Never made to happen.
39	- Change: throw on an error answer inside the existing `reported(...)` callback, and keep the sentence
40	  for no answer.
41	- **Needs more.** The callback hands the sheet only a link or nothing, so the sheet cannot show "ours",
42	  and it cannot show the existing "sign in again" sentence for the 401. Either needs a new outcome
43	  carried to the sheet.
44	
45	**Email sign-in: a refusal the app has no branch for.**
46	- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:313-314`. Any 4xx without a branch, and no answer, both show
47	  "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again."
48	- Whose: no answer is the person's network. A 4xx from our own server that the app does not expect is
49	  ours, since our code is on both ends. The local server (allauth 65.21.1) answered a probe like this:
50	  - a correct password for an address not yet confirmed: 401 with the sign-in flows;
51	  - too many tries at login: 429;
52	  - a code request for a deactivated account: 400 `account_inactive`.
53	
54	  The 401 and the 400 reach this branch today. The probe ran inside a transaction that was rolled
55	  back, and no email was sent. The app's own display of these was not driven.
56	- Change: one else-if, so a 4xx with no branch goes to the existing `unexpected(said)`.
57	- **Needs more.** Two of those answers are the person's and have no sentence: an address not yet
58	  confirmed (the 401), and a deactivated account. After the change they would be reported as ours.
59	
60	**Password sign-in: any 400 is "That password is wrong."**
61	- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:311-312`.
62	- Whose: the probe above answered 400 `username_password_mismatch` for a wrong password, for an
63	  unknown address and for an account with no password, and 400 `too_many_login_attempts` after five
64	  tries. Both are the person's, and the app has sentences for both. Any other 400 at login is ours.
65	- Change: an else-if on `username_password_mismatch`, keeping the existing too-many-tries branch and
66	  sending any other 400 to `unexpected(said)`.
67	- **Simple.**

118	- Where: `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:52-61` with `model_list_fault` (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:196-202`).

128	- Where: `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:91-104` and `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:340-342`. "Signing in didn't

# Each misrouted failure: a simple change, or more (2026-11-25)

Read only, on the app at `jusprin-dev` `9f485c3604` and the server at `master` `d9c224e114`. Nothing
was changed, built or run for this file. Each place in `error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` has one
entry, except the two Kenneth marked "Not to be fixed": the 120-second limit on a reply, and a
checkout that returns "succeeded" with the invoice unpaid. The list's place 21 holds seven separate
spots, and its places 26 and 27 hold two and four. Each of those spots has its own entry, so there are
50 entries in all. App paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, server paths under `web_ent/jusprin/`.

"Simple" here is the reading in the brief, not Kenneth's wording. The change is made at the place
itself by adding or removing a try/catch or an if/else, or by deleting handling. It uses only what the
code has today.

## Counts

- **Simple: 17.**
- **Needs more: 30.**
- **Nothing to change: 3.**
- **Never made to happen: 34.** This counts across the three groups above. It means the failure
  itself was never produced against the real thing, by me or in the evidence I have. A test with a
  fake counts as never made to happen.

The most common reasons a place needs more:
- the person's failure can only be told to them with words we do not have: a new sentence, or the
  "the system says" frame that went with the reversal;
- the failure repeats, every few seconds or on every press, so reporting it once needs a record of
  what was already reported;
- the page or callback gets only "worked or not", so telling "ours" apart from "no network" needs a
  new field.

## The app

**Credits and plans, Billing and usage, will not open.**
- Where: `Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:86-96`, the answer to the link request. Any answer other than 200 with a
  link, or no answer, shows "Couldn't load Credits and plans" (`:375`) with "Check your internet
  connection, then try again."
- Whose: an error answer from our server is ours, and no answer is the person's network. An ended
  sign-in (401) is the person's. Never made to happen.
- Change: throw on an error answer inside the existing `reported(...)` callback, and keep the sentence
  for no answer.
- **Needs more.** The callback hands the sheet only a link or nothing, so the sheet cannot show "ours",
  and it cannot show the existing "sign in again" sentence for the 401. Either needs a new outcome
  carried to the sheet.

**Email sign-in: a refusal the app has no branch for.**
- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:313-314`. Any 4xx without a branch, and no answer, both show
  "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again."
- Whose: no answer is the person's network. A 4xx from our own server that the app does not expect is
  ours, since our code is on both ends. The local server (allauth 65.21.1) answered a probe like this:
  - a correct password for an address not yet confirmed: 401 with the sign-in flows;
  - too many tries at login: 429;
  - a code request for a deactivated account: 400 `account_inactive`.

  The 401 and the 400 reach this branch today. The probe ran inside a transaction that was rolled
  back, and no email was sent. The app's own display of these was not driven.
- Change: one else-if, so a 4xx with no branch goes to the existing `unexpected(said)`.
- **Needs more.** Two of those answers are the person's and have no sentence: an address not yet
  confirmed (the 401), and a deactivated account. After the change they would be reported as ours.

**Password sign-in: any 400 is "That password is wrong."**
- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:311-312`.
- Whose: the probe above answered 400 `username_password_mismatch` for a wrong password, for an
  unknown address and for an account with no password, and 400 `too_many_login_attempts` after five
  tries. Both are the person's, and the app has sentences for both. Any other 400 at login is ours.
- Change: an else-if on `username_password_mismatch`, keeping the existing too-many-tries branch and
  sending any other 400 to `unexpected(said)`.
- **Simple.**

**Delete account.**
- Where: `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:143-163`. Any answer but 204 hands the page `false`, and the page
  shows "The account couldn't be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again."
  (`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:310`).
- Whose: an error answer from our server is ours, and no answer is the person's network. Never made to
  happen.
- Change: throw on an error answer inside the existing `reported(...)` callback.
- **Needs more.** The page gets only true or false, so it would still show the internet sentence under
  the report. Telling the two apart needs a new field in the answer to the page.

**Print report with no answer.**
- Where: `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:254-258`. Every answer the app does not expect is already thrown. Only
  "no answer at all" keeps the form's "check your connection" sentence.
- Whose: settled by Kenneth's "This error msg is reasonable", which covers a message shown when
  nothing answered.
- **Nothing to change.**

**Update check.**
- Where: `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:102-115` and `:126-136`. Any answer but 200, no answer, and a list
  the app cannot read all record a failure, shown as "Couldn't reach GitHub".
- Whose: GitHub's rate limit leaves the person doing the same as no network. Other error answers and
  an unreadable list are ours. GitHub's limit facts are from its documentation, not run.
- Change: throw inside the existing `reported(...)` callback for an error answer that is not the rate
  limit.
- **Needs more.** Two things are missing:
  - the check runs again on a timer and from the Check now button, so the report needs a record of
    "already reported in this run";
  - GitHub's error text names the person's IP address, so it cannot go into the report as it is.

**The AI panel will not start.**
- Where: `Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:237-241, :322-332, :385`. "The AI panel could not connect", with the
  reason and "Bridge traffic: …". It is logged only.
- Whose: a page that does not load or finish its handshake is ours. A Windows computer without WebView2
  is the person's. I made the panel fail in the real built app by pointing the page at a dead address.
- Change: report from `show_bridge_error`.
- **Needs more.** In that run the handshake timer fired again 20 s later, and Retry fires it again, so
  reporting once needs a record. A missing WebView2 needs its own sentence and a way to tell that
  the runtime is missing.

**Home will not start.**
- Where: `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:80, :85, :177`. Three sentences, all logged only.
- Whose: a packaged page missing from the build (`:80`) is ours, and so is a local page that fails to
  load (`:177`). "The system web view could not be created" (`:85`) may be a missing WebView2, which
  is the person's. Never made to happen.
- Change: `report_unexpected_error` at `:80` and `:177`.
- **Needs more**, for `:85` only: a missing WebView2 needs its own sentence. The other two lines are
  simple.

**JusPrin's model list.**
- Where: `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:52-61` with `model_list_fault` (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:196-202`).
  A 4xx from our server, or no answer, shows "Signed in · AI unavailable … Try again in a moment".
  Only a 5xx is reported.
- Whose: a 4xx from our own server is ours, apart from an ended sign-in and the "update the app"
  answer, which already have handling. No answer is the person's network. Never made to happen.
- Change: one if at the call site, for an account profile only. A 4xx that is not a 401 and not an
  update answer throws.
- **Simple.**

**Browser sign-in does not finish.**
- Where: `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:91-104` and `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:340-342`. "Signing in didn't
  finish. Nothing was saved. Try again." It is logged only.
- Whose: made to happen with probes against OrcaSlicer's sign-in job.
  - A port another program holds gives "bind: Address already in use", which is the person's.
  - Our token exchange answering 400, answering 500, or not running at all gives the same "Unknown
    error" in all three cases. Those three are ours.
  - The person declining in the browser gives a different message, and that one is the person's.
- **Needs more.** The three that are ours cannot be told from one another, or from other failures,
  without a field in OrcaSlicer's `OAuthJob` result. That is an OrcaSlicer-owned file, and the field
  is with Kenneth.

**Autosave.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:351` and `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:616`. Disk full, a folder that
  cannot be written, and our own bug all show "Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.", and the
  system's reason is dropped.
- Whose: the system refusing to write the person's projects folder is theirs. Anything else is ours.
  Made to happen in the shell harness, with a full projects folder, one that cannot be written, and a
  failing writer.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the system's words shown with who said them, which needs a
  frame string. The save retries every 2 s, so reporting ours once needs a record per project.

**Export, restore, version history.**
- Where: `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:161-168` and its two neighbours. "The project couldn't be exported.
  Try again." and two like it. The reason is logged only.
- Whose: a folder the person picked that the system refuses is theirs. Anything else is ours. Made to
  happen in the harness, from the real File menu.
- Change: rethrow for anything but the system's refusal.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the system's words and a frame string.

**Opening a project.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:952-954`. The same "The project couldn't be opened. Try again."
  covers three owners.
- Whose:
  - a project another JusPrin window holds is the person's;
  - the current project failing to save because the system refused is the person's;
  - a damaged project is ours.

  All three were made to happen in the harness.
- **Needs more.** The other-window sentence is with Kenneth. The system's refusal needs the frame
  string. Only the damaged project, which would be a rethrow, is simple.

**A project with an interrupted chat restore disappears from Home.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:444`. The store refuses a project whose restore marker is
  still there ("requires recovery"), and the project is missing from Home and cannot be opened.
- Whose: ours. Made to happen by ending the app at the instant a real restore wrote its marker, then
  starting it again.
- **Needs more.** Deleting the refusal opens the project, but the open chat and the model can be on
  different versions. Making them match again needs new code that finishes the restore.

**The projects folder cannot be read.**
- Where: `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1019`. "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
  The reason is dropped.
- Whose: the system refusing the person's folder is theirs. Anything else is ours. Made to happen at
  startup with the projects folder replaced by a plain file.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the frame string. The listing runs every second, so
  reporting ours once needs a record.

**Printer profiles shipped with the app fail to install or read.**
- Where:
  - `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:229-231`: logged only;
  - `:341-345`: a printer is marked "JusPrin couldn't load this preset";
  - `PrinterSetup/SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:83-86`: shown as "The printer profiles could not be read: …".
- Whose: ours. The code's own comment says this fails only on a broken install. Made to happen in the
  harness with profiles that cannot be installed.
- Change: throw at each of the three spots in place of the log line or the marked reason.
- **Simple.**

**Save on a proposal card.**
- Where: `AgentUI/src/components/ProposalCard.tsx:31-32`. "The action failed.", and the failure goes to
  the AI as a tool result.
- Whose: the system refusing the preset file is the person's. Anything else is ours. Only made to
  happen with fakes, in C++ and page tests.
- **Needs more.** The card gets only the tool's state. Showing the system's words needs a field and the
  frame string, and reporting ours needs the press handled as the person's click, not as a tool call.

**Tool failures in the app's own work reach us only with automatic reports on.**
- Where: `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:714-717`.
- Whose: this is the rule's own exception. AGENTS.md says such a failure is reported "only if the
  person has turned automatic reports on".
- **Nothing to change.**

**The local tool server's helper tells the outside AI client to open JusPrin when JusPrin is open.**
- Where: `Mcp/Bridge/Bridge.cpp:152-162`. JusPrin answering its liveness probe with an error leads to
  "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again."
- Whose: ours. The settled answer is that the helper tells the client the truth and logs, with no
  Sentry. Never made to happen.
- Change: an else-if that hands the client the error JusPrin itself sent, in place of the offline
  sentence.
- **Simple.**

**History cleanup warning.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:455`. Logged only.
- Whose: ours. Never made to happen against the real store.
- **Needs more.** It runs after every save, so reporting it once needs a record.

**A damaged printer-facts file is emptied with no word.**
- Where: `Workspace/PrinterFactsStore.cpp:56-80`. The file is moved aside, and `corrupt()` records it,
  but nothing ever reads `corrupt()`.
- Whose: ours, since the file is the app's own. Never made to happen.
- Change: throw where it now records `m_corrupt`.

content.text:
The handoff note still lists 42 places as not done. I think 26 of them are real: a failure goes to the wrong one, or never reaches anyone. Twelve of those 26 can happen to someone doing something ordinary, and the other 14 are rare. The remaining 16 aren't real issues. This comes from reading the notes and the code; most of these places have never been made to happen.

**Real and likely to be met (12):**
1. Signing in with a password on an address not yet confirmed, or on a deactivated account, says "Try again." Trying again can't help.
2. Autosave on a full disk, or into a folder that can't be written, drops the system's reason and retries forever.
3. Opening a project that another JusPrin window holds says "Try again."
4. Exporting to a folder the system refuses, such as a locked or full card, says "Try again" without the reason.
5. A Moonraker printer that needs an API key is shown as "isn't answering."
6. A chat that is too long names no next step.
7. A plan whose renewal payment was declined: the chat says "you have 0 credits" while the page says the plan renews.
8. When our server fails, Credits and plans (and Billing and usage) tells the person to check their internet.
9. Delete account does the same.
10. When the AI panel fails to start, it is only logged, so we never hear about it.
11. When our token step fails at the end of browser sign-in, it shows as "Unknown error" and is only logged.
12. An AI tool exporting to a folder that can't be written is reported as our failure, when it's the person's.

**Real but rare (14):**
- On a broken install or a damaged app file: shipped profiles failing during an OrcaSlicer import; a damaged printer-facts file emptied silently; a damaged project, or a failed restore or version history, shown as "Try again."
- A project that disappears from Home when the app ends in the middle of a chat restore. This is a real bug, bigger than a question of who gets the failure.
- A printer connection test that throws ends the app. I confirmed the path in the code: the job's end rethrows, and OrcaSlicer's last handler rethrows again. No known trigger yet.
- The projects folder can't be read. OrcaSlicer's settings file can't be read. Save on a proposal card fails. An attachment can't be read. Home won't start (two of its three causes are ours and only logged; the third is a missing WebView2 on Windows).
- The history cleanup after each save fails. A kept G-code file changed on disk. Both are only logged.
- Server: a paid Chargebee event for a plan missing from our settings grants nothing and says nothing.
- JusPrin 1: any Chargebee error silently drops the Obico Pro discount. The plan read answers 500 and never reports.

**Not real (16):**
- **Can't happen today.** Any other 400 at password sign-in: allauth answers the same way for every password failure. A 4xx on JusPrin's model list: our server never sends one there. The tool-server helper disagreeing with the app: they ship together.
- **What the person does is already right.** A GitHub rate limit sharing "Couldn't reach GitHub": the person waits either way, and the rule gives two such causes one sentence. A token for the wrong client is told "Sign in", which fixes it. A link our cache lost and one opened late both end with opening the page again.
- **Theoretical.** A database conflict other than the print's own report. The server failing to read an uploaded photo. A cancelled JusPrin 1 checkout, never seen in 90 days.
- **Owner not known yet.** A dropped file the page can't read. A provider refusing the person's own content. The printer window's "Nothing answered", which is often true.
- **Not about who gets a failure.** A message staying charged when the provider fails is a billing policy. The JusPrin 1 webhook staying quiet is right, because ordinary first purchases reach it. The web link address was left alone on purpose.
- **Deleting an account when Chargebee can't find the subscription.** I disagree with the note here. The deletion asks the same Chargebee site that issued the plan, so a subscription Chargebee doesn't have can't charge a card. Returning quietly looks correct to me.

Most of the 12 common ones need a new sentence from you or a new field before they can be fixed.

Should I start making the 12 common ones happen in the real app, one at a time — yes, or not now?

"""Signing in to JusPrin from inside the desktop app, by email.

The app talks to allauth's own API for apps (allauth.headless, the "app"
client): it asks for a code and confirms it, or logs in with a password. Only
those views are mounted (urls.py), not the whole API, so nothing else that
allauth.headless serves, such as its sign-up without the website's reCAPTCHA,
becomes reachable. Between steps the app carries allauth's session token. A
finished sign-in ends in what the browser sign-in ends in: an OAuth2 access and
refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application (TokenStrategy).

Two things allauth does not do here. It looks an address up across every
syndicate, so the code request looks it up in the request's syndicate as the
website does (users_by_email). And it sends no code to an
address without an account, so the code request makes that account first, with
no usable password, as the website's sign-up would; confirming the code marks
the address verified.
"""
from allauth.account import signals
from allauth.account.adapter import get_adapter
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from allauth.account.utils import setup_user_email
from allauth.core import context, ratelimit
from allauth.headless.account import views as headless
from allauth.headless.account.inputs import RequestLoginCodeInput
from allauth.headless.constants import Client
from allauth.headless.tokens.strategies.sessions import SessionTokenStrategy
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from oauth2_provider.models import Application
from oauth2_provider.settings import oauth2_settings
        # RequestLoginCodeForm.clean_email, with the account looked up in the
        # request's syndicate and an inactive one refused rather than
        # passed over, so no second account is made beside it.
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        if not email:
            return email
        request = context.request
        if not ratelimit.consume(request, action='request_login_code', key=email.lower()):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('too_many_login_attempts')
        users = users_by_email(email, syndicate_from_request(request))
        if users and not any(user.is_active for user in users):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        active = [user for user in users if user.is_active]
        self._user = active[0] if active else None
        return email


class RequestLoginCodeView(headless.RequestLoginCodeView):
    input_class = SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.input._user is None:
            self.input._user = _new_account(request, self.input.cleaned_data['email'])
        return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)


def _new_account(request, email: str):
    """Makes the account for an address that has none, as the website's sign-up
    does (the account adapter, then the address as an unverified primary
    EmailAddress), with no usable password. Confirming the code verifies the
    address."""
    adapter = get_adapter(request)
    with transaction.atomic():
        user = adapter.new_user(request)
        user.email = email
        user.syndicate = syndicate_from_request(request)
        adapter.populate_username(request, user)
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        setup_user_email(request, user, [EmailAddress(email=email)])
    signals.user_signed_up.send(sender=User, request=request, user=user)
    """Whether the same person pays for Obico Premium: an account in Obico's own
    syndicate under this account's email with an active subscription that
    Chargebee bills (a non-empty external_id). That leaves out the free trial
    every new account starts (start_free_trial) and the free pro-comp plans,
    as JusPrin 1 does. A JusPrin 2 account's own email is always verified: it
    signs in by an emailed code or by Google."""

    from app.models import Syndicate
    from app_ent.models import Subscription

# Serves the JusPrin v2 gateway's streaming endpoints beside obico-server's
# own ASGI application; see web_ent/jusprin/v2/asgi.py.
ASGI_APPLICATION = 'jusprin.v2.asgi.application'

# TSD's own settings ###

CHARGEBEE_API_KEY = os.environ.get('CHARGEBEE_API_KEY')
CHARGEBEE_SITE = os.environ.get('CHARGEBEE_SITE')

ACCOUNT_ADAPTER = 'jusprin.v2.account_adapter.AccountAdapter'
ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_REDIRECT_URL = '/ent/accounts/welcome/'
ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION = 'optional'
ACCOUNT_EMAIL_SUBJECT_PREFIX = '✅ '
ACCOUNT_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION_AUTHENTICATED_REDIRECT_URL = '/ent/new_user_survey/'
# allauth's login by code, used only by the JusPrin app's email sign-in
# (jusprin/v2/sign_in.py); the website's pages for it are not served
# (urls_ent.py). Six digits, ten minutes, five tries; the app asks again for
# a new code rather than using allauth's resend.
ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_ENABLED = True
ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_FORMAT = {'numeric': True, 'length': 6, 'dashed': False}
ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_TIMEOUT = 10 * 60
ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
# allauth merges these over its own defaults: codes sent, 5 per address and 20
# per client IP an hour.
ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMITS = {'request_login_code': '20/h/ip,5/h/key'}
# allauth's API for apps, as the JusPrin app's email sign-in uses it.
HEADLESS_CLIENTS = ('app',)
HEADLESS_TOKEN_STRATEGY = 'jusprin.v2.sign_in.TokenStrategy'
# The code email in JusPrin's words, ahead of allauth's own template.
TEMPLATES[0]['DIRS'].insert(0, os.path.join(BASE_DIR, 'jusprin/templates/allauth'))
# JusPrin 2's server text in the app's language rather than the browser's, for
# JusPrin 2's paths only; see jusprin/v2/language.py.
MIDDLEWARE.insert(MIDDLEWARE.index('django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware') + 1,
                  'jusprin.v2.language.jusprin_language_middleware')
TEMPLATE_LAYOUT = "layout_ent.html"
IS_ENT = True
